lines: In this final episode: how you will be assessed, and the Qualification Shoot.
You need to be assessed against the outcomes of this Unit Standard in order to be declared competent.

scenes.heading: What you must be capable of
bullets: Basic inspection and maintenance for safe use

lines.text: People credited with this unit standard are capable of handling a handgun.
Using a handgun.
And carrying out basic inspection and maintenance of a handgun for safe use.

lines: You may be assessed on either a revolver or a pistol, or both.

scenes.heading: Two theory exams

lines.text: Exam one is the Formative Assessment, an open book exam at the back of the manual.

lines: It may be completed at home, with no time limit, and you may ask for assistance.
It must already be completed when you attend your booked sessions.

lines.text: Exam two is the Summative Assessment, a closed book exam with a one hour time limit.

lines: It is completed in the classroom, under the supervision of an accredited PFTC registered Assessor, and no assistance may be given.
Both are completed in black ink, and no correction fluid is allowed.

scenes.definition: Where your Assessor records the practical skills and tasks you perform. The last task is the Qualification Shoot.
lines: After your practical training, you will perform various practical skills and tasks.
Your Assessor records these on an Observation Checklist.
The last one you will perform is the Qualification Shoot.

scenes.heading: Observation Checklist: items 1 to 7
bullets: 1. Identify and designate a safe direction
3. Load, safe direction, finger off the trigger
4. Demonstrate the operation of the safety catch
5. Unload, safe direction, finger off the trigger
6. Make the firearm safe from an unknown condition
7. Load to a safe carry condition

lines.text: One: identify and designate a safe direction, so you and the Assessor agree on what is safe or unsafe.
Two: identify an alternative safe direction.
Three: load the relevant firearm while maintaining a safe direction, with the finger off the trigger.
Four: demonstrate how the safety catch works on the firearm that you are using.
Five: unload the relevant firearm while maintaining a safe direction, with the finger off the trigger.
Six: the Assessor loads the firearm to a condition unknown to you, and you make it safe.
Seven: load the firearm to a safe carry condition.

scenes.caption: Items 8 and 9: identify ammunition by calibre
lines: Eight: an ammunition identification task.
The Assessor gives you at least two different types of ammunition, which you identify by calibre.
Nine: identify the correct ammunition for the relevant firearm.
The Assessor provides at least three types of ammunition, and one must be the correct ammunition for the firearm.

scenes.heading: Observation Checklist: items 10 to 13
bullets: 12. Explain the dangers of oil in the barrel

lines.text: Ten: identify and rectify malfunctions, which the Assessor simulates with your firearm, using dummy ammunition, empty cases, or both.
Eleven: carry out a safety inspection with the relevant firearm.
Twelve: explain the dangers of oil or any other obstructions in the barrel.

lines: While doing so, explain or demonstrate the correct method of cleaning and maintaining the relevant firearm.

lines.text: Thirteen: demonstrate the fundamentals of shooting.

lines: That's stance, grip, trigger squeeze, breathing, sight alignment, sight picture and follow through.

rule.text: The trigger finger was kept off the trigger at all relevant times when handling the firearm.

lines: Fourteen: your Assessor checks that your trigger finger was kept off the trigger at all relevant times, during all the exercises.

scenes.heading: 15. The Qualification Shoot
lines: Fifteen: successfully complete the Qualification Shoot.

lines.text: You shoot from a distance of 7 metres.
In the standing position.
You load and fire 10 shots at your own target, in your own time, with no time limit.
The target is A3 size.
lines.say: The target is A three size.

lines.text: And the pass mark is 10 out of 10, which is 100 percent.

scenes.caption: Dead-resting, which is not allowed, and the two-handed standing position
lines: You may not dead-rest the firearm during the Qualification Shoot, as the shooter on the left is doing.
On the right is a two-handed standing position, the position you will be required to use.
You must complete the entire Qualification Shoot unassisted.

lines.text: That includes, but is not limited to, loading and unloading, use of PPE, range rules, range commands and safety procedures.
lines.say: That includes, but is not limited to, loading and unloading, use of P P E, range rules, range commands and safety procedures.

lines: The book says to expect to shoot at least 40 rounds of ammunition in total during your course.

rule.text: A safe muzzle direction was maintained at all times during the above exercises.

lines: And sixteen: a safe muzzle direction was maintained at all times, during the practical exercises and the Qualification Shoot.

scenes.heading: After your assessment
bullets: Portfolio of Evidence: kept for six years
A second assessment, free of charge

lines.text: Your Assessor compiles a Portfolio of Evidence, kept on file at the Training Centre for six years.

lines: Make sure the copy of your ID is certified, because an uncertified copy cannot be accepted.

lines.text: If you are unsuccessful, you will be given a second assessment free of charge, paying only for consumables.
And if you are unsatisfied with your assessment, you are entitled to appeal.

scenes.question: In the Qualification Shoot, how many of your 10 shots must hit the A3 target?
lines: In the Qualification Shoot, how many of your 10 shots must hit the target?
Pause the video if you need a moment.
reveal: The pass mark is 10 out of 10, from 7 metres, on an A3 target, with no time limit.

scenes.question: Which exam is closed book, with a one hour time limit?
lines: Which exam is closed book, with a one hour time limit?
reveal: It is completed in the classroom, under the supervision of an accredited PFTC registered Assessor.

points: Formative: open book. Summative: closed book
Qualification Shoot: 7 m, A3, 10 out of 10
No dead-resting; finger off; safe muzzle
lines: So, two theory exams: the open book Formative, and the closed book Summative.
Your Assessor works through the 16 items of the Observation Checklist.
The Qualification Shoot is 10 shots from 7 metres on an A3 target, and you need all 10.
No dead-resting, finger off the trigger, and a safe muzzle direction at all times.
Good luck with your assessment.
